Hi Kimberly —

Thanks — we’re keen. Quick question: when I accepted Option A in my calendar (11:00 JST / 13:00 AEDT), Google Calendar labeled it as Thu Dec 17 for our Sydney teammates even though the invite shows Dec 16 in the body. That caused some confusion in our scheduling channel.

Ben / Marcus — looping you both for a quick fix. Amrita hit the classic local-date disparity: Google is rendering the invite date differently for Sydney (AEDT+11) than the body labels I sent (which were written with the local-labels but not explicit UTC).

Plan I suggest:
1) Re-send a single confirmed invite that shows the UTC time and all three local labels in the body and the subject. For example: \"Dec 16 02:00 UTC — 10:00 SGT / 11:00 JST / 13:00 AEDT\" so attendees see the canonical instant.
2) Attach an explicit .ics we generate (redwood-demo.ics) that sets the DTSTART/DTEND with TZID=UTC and an X-ALT-DESC listing the three local labels.
3) Offer a fallback slot that keeps the meeting inside normal office hours for SYD (13:00 AEDT) in case someone’s calendar client mis-parses DST.

Ben — can you generate the ICS and a short one-slide note explaining the UTC anchor? Marcus — please hold Option A at 13:00 AEDT on my end while I confirm. I’ll also include a note advising attendees to view the invite in their local timezone and to check the ICS if their calendar client shows a different date.

Thanks —
Kimberly
